hints.title: Distinct Element Filtering
hints.text: Any duplicates must be replaced since elements in a continuous array are strictly unique. Deduplicate and sort.

hints.title: Fixed Length Target Window
hints.text: If unique[left] is chosen as the minimum element of the continuous array, the maximum allowable value is unique[left] plus n minus one.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Sliding Window
hints.text: Advance right pointer while unique[right] is within the allowable window. Number of operations equals total array length n minus window width.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minOperations(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        unique = sorted(set(nums))
        ans = n
        r = 0
        for l in range(len(unique)):
            while r < len(unique) and unique[r] <= unique[l] + n - 1:
                r += 1
            count = r - l
            ans = min(ans, n - count)
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting unique elements of array of length N
complexity.notes: Sliding window advances each pointer at most once over unique elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all potential continuous intervals takes quadratic or worse time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Deduplicating and sorting allows linear two-pointer scanning.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert continuous condition to fixed range constraint and apply sliding window.
